findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a stacked item is closed after its parent has been squash-merged and both the item and default branch refreshed the timing file.
The approved item is: “Merging the default branch into an item resolves a conflict in .test_durations alone by keeping both sides' entries, with no builder round, and any other conflict still stops as before.” The replay path in `src/forge/close.py:707-727` refuses a timing-only conflict before reaching this resolver. Close and land therefore still direct the user to a work round for stacked tasks and follow-up fixes.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - the default branch deletes or renames a test while a parallel item refreshes the timing inventory.
The union restores the deleted test's timing from the item's older inventory. New evidence for the union ruling is that `tests/test_ci_timing_inventory.py:25-27` rejects timing keys that no longer correspond to collected tests; the isolated passing check in the proof list does not exercise a merged inventory. The resulting pull request fails its tests and needs a repair round despite the automatic merge.
Adds work: reconcile deleted test IDs with the inventory check; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 4.
findings.title: Disputed keep the timing union: obsolete test entries make CI fail

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a client's pre-commit hook rejects the combined tree while `forge work` resolves a timing conflict.
The failed commit raises out of the resolver without aborting or finishing the merge. `src/forge/worker.py:110-111` then refuses every subsequent work round because `MERGE_HEAD` remains, while the initial error directs the user to `forge doctor`. The item requires manual Git recovery before a worker can continue.
Adds work: handle merge-commit failures and leave a usable checkout; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 2.
findings.title: Handle a rejected automatic merge commit in forge work

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a stacked item reaches close after its parent lands.
All five listed cases create an ordinary fix through `env.start_fix`; none gives it a `stacked_on` parent or exercises the replay path at `src/forge/close.py:707-737`. The named proof can therefore pass while a timing-only conflict still blocks stacked tasks and follow-up fixes. Add an entry-point case for that history.
findings.title: Gate: timing-conflict resolution for stacked items

why: When several items run in parallel, each one that adds tests refreshes .test_durations, so every later merge of main stops on a conflict in that file and a builder round or a person has to resolve it
